I have a very simple AGI test. ChapterPal has a fully automatic content ingestion pipeline. It can take a PDF or an arXiv projet, a paper or a thousand page book with thousands tables, illustrations, and equations, and convert these to a nearly perfect Markdown with all the tables, figures, equations and other semantic blocks perfectly converted.

I have enough cash to ingest my entire pipeline that has about 150,000 items overnight and get the world's biggest collection of knowledge in a format optimal for self learning with an AI tutor.

What my pipeline cannot do though is to validate that the conversion is perfect. Currently about 20% of the converted items have minor conversion issues here and there like leaked LaTeX, wrong year, or an entirely wrong PDF file used for conversion.

No AI can reliably detect all issues, fix them, and publish an item on my behalf. It either misses some issues or fixes something that wasn't broken.

So, I'm the bottleneck.

As soon as such an AI that can replace me as a pre-publishing validator/fixer is created, this will be the moment of singularity for ChapterPal and I will say that AGI has been finally built.

Selling VCRs back in the 1980s taught me the market doesn’t listen to me.

But back then Silicon Valley nerds usually bought VHS because of content.

And same will be true in the glasses.

In other words, the questions for early adopters will be “do you use them every day or throw them into the drawer with the other devices and leave it there?”

items.content_html:
Introduction to Computer Science by Jean-Claude Franchitti (2024) is in @ChapterPal's collection of open books.

Ths is a broad textbook for introductory college students and prospective software practitioners who require a comprehensive grounding in the discipline.

The text assumes minimal prior technical background, beginning with foundational problem-solving concepts before systematically advancing through low-level hardware structures, systems software, full-stack application development, and cloud-scale architectures.

Its scope encompasses both fundamental theory and applied industry practice, balancing the technical mechanics of computation with discussions of social responsibility, algorithmic fairness, and data governance.

Read with an AI tutor: https://t.co/2agLZPD7l5

All books on ChapterPal are free to read with a free accout.
